newsitem.title: USA: Moderate earthquakes rattle Los Angeles.
newsitem.headline: Moderate earthquakes rattle Los Angeles.

text.p: Two moderate earthquakes shook the Los Angeles area early on Saturday but there were no initial reports of damage or injury.

A spokesman for the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) said the first temblor, which struck at 3:37 a.m. PDT (6:37 a.m. EDT) (1037 GMT) had a magnitude of 5.0 on the Richter scale. The second quake hit five minutes later with a magnitude of 4.0.

Caltech seismologist Steve Bryant said both quakes were aftershocks to the 1994 Northridge earthquake, which had a 6.8-magnitude, killed more than 50 people and caused billions of dollars in damage throughout the Los Angeles area.

The two aftershocks were centred in the Simi Valley region of Los Angeles and caused emergency services to go into an "earthquake mode." Fire departments moved trucks out of their stations and police helicopters took to the air to survey the area for damage.
Police and fire department spokesmen said the measures were precautionary and no damage was found.
